headline: 40 clear at the top —
Wirtz decides he likes it here
body: A week after his first goal of the season, Wirtz goes again: a goal and an assist against Man Utd for 14. Strand Larsen adds 10, it's a joint-top 47, and the lead over Umar is out to 40.
The only blemish is in goal. Pickford starts for 1 while Tzolakis gets 10 on the bench. Nobody's complaining at 40 clear, but the Heung Min boys will want that one back.

headline: Switches keepers —
and the other one scores 7
body: Umar finally takes the hint about his keeper. Verbruggen comes in and gets 2. Kinsky, now on the bench, gets 7. The goalkeeping curse is real, and it has his number.
Silva's 8 leads a solid back line, but Haaland's 2 doesn't help much. 39 points, Imad's 40 clear, and Los Porros are now 26 behind. Second place needs watching too.

headline: The revamp lands —
and McBurnie's 13 sits on the bench
body: The promised new blood arrives: Guéhi and McBurnie come in from Kavinu, with Colwill and Gonzalo going the other way. Pedro Porro's 11 leads a joint-top 47.
The catch: McBurnie scores 13 on debut and watches all of it from the bench. 21 points left in the dugout, the most in the league. Imagine the score if Rihab had trusted the new signing.

headline: Up to 4th —
but check who won the trade
body: Split the G sneak into 4th, two points above Vidhun. Mukiele repays the waiver claim with 8 on debut, and Madueke matches him.
Then there's the trade. Colwill and Gonzalo arrive and manage 1 between them, while McBurnie scores 13 for Rihab, who doesn't even start him. Somehow both sides lose that one.

headline: Hill 14, Tarkowski −4 —
down to 5th by two points
body: James Hill has a week to frame: an assist, a clean sheet, max bonus and 14 points. Tarkowski undoes a chunk of it with -4, and Saliba starts without playing a minute.
32 points and the slide continues. Last week's card said one more week like this and he'd be looking at 4th from below. Split the G go past by 2. Here we are.

headline: Found the waiver button —
and back up to 6th
body: Last week's card asked if Dulaj had ever found the waiver button. He has. Justin, Samithu's cast-off, arrives for Thiaw and posts 4 from the bench.
Calvert-Lewin's 9 leads a steady 41, enough to climb back above Munir into 6th. Delap comes back down to earth after his brace, but nobody's complaining.

headline: 59 to 29 —
the comedown hits
body: From the week's best to 29 in seven days. McGinn and Cherki manage 1 each, two defenders blank, and Asspine end joint second-lowest of GW11.
Belloumi's 7 is the bright spot, and Ajayi scores 6 on the bench just to rub it in. Dulaj goes back past him, and Munir starts GW12 in 7th.

headline: Message received —
a striker, finally
body: Someone clearly told him. Ometh signs a forward, Muniz, and he scores 8 on debut. Solanke wakes up with 7, and an attack that managed 1 last week brings in 16.
Roefs is excellent again with 11, and 44 is the third-best score of the week. 8th doesn't budge, though: Munir is still 11 ahead.

headline: Gap holds at 8 —
but nobody's comfortable
body: 29 points, but for once the keeper call costs nothing: Lammens and Trafford both get 2. Kerkez and Ajer carry it with 6 each, and new signing Alysson chips in.
Sandaru only manages 28, so the gap at the bottom of the overall table goes from 7 to 8. One more point of breathing room. The big forfeit is still lurking.

headline: Lowest score of the week —
one gameweek left to dodge the wall
body: 28, the lowest of GW11. Kluivert does his bit with 9, but Costinha starts and goes -2, and Bruno Fernandes comes back down from 10 to 2.
Sandaru went into the week bottom of the forfeit table, and this doesn't help. One gameweek left in the block, and the wall is getting closer.
